title: Message Basics
description: Learn message structure, headers, correlation IDs, and message formats.

data.text: Messages are the fundamental unit of asynchronous communication. Understanding message structure, headers, correlation IDs, and formats is essential for building reliable distributed systems.

terms.definition: A unit of data exchanged between services asynchronously.
Metadata attached to a message (routing, correlation, timestamps).
A unique identifier that traces a request across services.
The actual payload of the message.

data.text: A message typically has a header (metadata) and a body (payload). The header contains routing information, timestamps, and correlation IDs. The body contains the actual data.
Correlation IDs trace a single request across multiple services. They are generated at the entry point and propagated through headers in every service call and message.

items: Exactly-once: Message delivered exactly once (hardest to achieve)

items.question: What is the difference between message ID and correlation ID?
items.answer: Message ID identifies a single message. Correlation ID traces a request across multiple messages and services.

items.question: Should I use JSON or Protobuf?
items.answer: JSON for simplicity and debugging; Protobuf for performance and compactness.

items.question: How do I ensure exactly-once delivery?
items.answer: Use idempotent consumers and deduplication. True exactly-once is hard; at-least-once with idempotency is the practical approach.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Correlation IDs trace requests across services
Choose message format based on performance and tooling needs
data.takeaway: Well-structured messages with correlation IDs are the foundation of reliable async systems.
